:::{#rem-negate-quantifiers}
#### How the two quantifier laws relate

De Morgan's laws for a [universal quantifier](#thm-negate-quantifiers) and an [existential quantifier](#thm-negate-existential)
are one rule seen from each side:
negating a [quantifier](#def-quantifier) swaps $\forall$ and $\exists$
and moves the [negation](#def-not) onto the [predicate](#def-predicate).
De Morgan's laws for a [conjunction](#thm-de-morgan-logic) and a [disjunction](#thm-de-morgan-disjunction) of two propositions pair up the same way,
and the quantifier laws extend them from two propositions to a whole [set](#def-set) of them.

:::
